cards.text: Jeremiah the prophet sent a letter with the LORD's word to the exiles in Babylon (Jeremiah 29:1). Now the word of the LORD comes to him again. And it starts with a job for Jeremiah.

cards.question: The LORD, the God of Israel, gives Jeremiah a job. What does He tell him to do with all the words He's spoken to him?

cards.text: Write it ALL down. Not a sticky note on the fridge, friend. A BOOK. Because the LORD says the days are coming, and He's about to tell Jeremiah what they'll bring.

cards.question: The days are coming when the LORD will do what for His people Israel and Judah?

answers.text: Leave them in Babylon for good

cards.question: The LORD will bring them back to the land He gave their fathers, and they will ___ it.

cards.text: These are the words the LORD spoke about Israel and Judah. And first, He describes a sound: "A cry of panic is heard—a cry of terror, not of peace."
Then the LORD asks, "Can a male give birth?" Friend, I'm a cookie stamper, and even I know that one. NO.

cards.question: The LORD sees every man with his hands on his stomach, like a woman in ___, and every face turned pale.

cards.text: "How awful that day will be! None will be like it!" It's the time of Jacob's distress. Jacob here means his people, Israel, the family that came from Jacob.

cards.question: Jacob's time of distress is so awful that it finishes him off for good.

cards.text: Then the LORD of Hosts says He'll break the yoke off their necks and tear off their bonds. I spent years stuck at the back of a junk drawer, friend, so I know EXACTLY how good that sounds.

cards.question: With the yoke broken and the bonds torn off, what does the LORD promise His people?

answers.text: No more strangers will enslave them
They will never have to work again
They will rule over all the nations

cards.question: Instead of serving strangers, the LORD's people will serve the LORD their God and ___ their king.

cards.text: A king the LORD will raise up for them. Then He speaks straight to His people, calling them "O Jacob My servant" and "O Israel."

cards.question: The LORD tells Jacob not to be afraid, because He will save him out of a distant place.
When Jacob comes home from the land of captivity, what will he return to?

cards.text: "For I am with you to save you, declares the LORD." Then He talks about the nations where He scattered His people.

cards.question: The LORD will completely destroy the nations He scattered His people to. What about His own people?

answers.text: He will not completely destroy them
He will leave them among the nations

cards.question: Since the LORD is saving His people, He will let them go unpunished.

cards.text: Then the LORD says, "Your injury is incurable; your wound is grievous." No one to plead their cause, no remedy, no recovery, and friend, this is NOT a slap-on-a-bandage-and-walk-it-off situation.

cards.question: There's no one to plead their cause. So what about all their "lovers"?

answers.text: They have come to rescue them
They have paid to free them

cards.question: The LORD says He has struck His people as an enemy would because of their great iniquity and numerous sins.

cards.text: "Why do you cry out over your wound? Your pain has no cure!" Friend, that's the checkup where the doctor pulls up a chair. But then the LORD says one word, "Nevertheless," and everything turns.

cards.question: Nevertheless, what happens to everyone who devoured, plundered and raided the LORD's people?

answers.text: The same thing happens to them
They are made rulers over them

cards.question: The wound with no cure? The LORD says He will restore their health and heal their wounds.
The LORD says why He'll heal Zion, His people. What's the reason?

answers.text: They call her an outcast no one cares for
Her old allies finally asked Him to
She healed her own wounds first

cards.text: "I will restore the fortunes of Jacob’s tents and have compassion on his dwellings." Then the LORD turns to the city, and I'm leaning in so far my gold base is tipping.

cards.question: The LORD says the city will never be rebuilt.
Remember that cry of panic? Now the LORD says thanksgiving will come from them, and a sound of ___.

cards.text: The LORD will multiply them, and they won't be decreased. He'll honor them, and they won't be belittled, and friend, NOBODY knows belittled like a stamper shoved under the takeout menus at the back of a junk drawer.
Their children will be as in days of old, and He'll punish all their oppressors. Friend, that's not a comeback, that's a whole COMEBACK TOUR.

cards.question: The LORD also speaks of their leader and ruler. Where will he come from?

cards.text: The LORD will bring this leader near to Him, "for who would dare on his own to approach Me?" Then the LORD says, "And you will be My people, and I will be your God."
But then the storm of the LORD goes out with fury. A whirlwind comes swirling down, and I'm holding my chef's hat on with BOTH ends of my mustache.

cards.question: The whirlwind of the LORD comes swirling down upon the heads of the ___.
The fierce anger of the LORD will turn back before He has fully accomplished the purposes of His heart.

cards.text: "In the days to come you will understand this." Then the LORD says what will be true at that time, and friend, I've got my nose pressed flat against the oven glass.

cards.question: At that time, the LORD says He will be the God of whom?

cards.text: And we'll pull this batch out of the oven right there for now. Trust me, friend, the LORD is NOT done talking to Jeremiah.

findings.problem: The last sentence says that the word starts with a job for Jeremiah, which uses Jeremiah 30:2, but the card cites only Jeremiah 30:1. The citation should extend through the verse that mentions the job.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Even treating the quoted exclamations as one unit, the card adds a sentence about Jacob's distress and another explaining who Jacob represents. That makes at least three units on a non-opening story card.

findings.problem: Nothing in the earlier cards identifies the promised king, so David cannot be reasoned out rather than Solomon or Saul. The blank asks for unseen wording using prior Bible knowledge or luck, rather than testing a meaning supported by the earlier cards.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
